result.summary: The food delivery home screen is mostly well-structured, but there is a clear data formatting bug ('€NaN delivery') and several layout/clipping issues in the horizontal carousel and category chip row. The second 'Popular right now' card is also cut off with an inconsistent favorite button style.

issues.description: The 'Smash Bros Burgers' card shows '€NaN delivery' instead of a real delivery fee, indicating an unhandled null/undefined value in the price formatting logic.
issues.suggestion: Guard the currency formatter against null/NaN values and fall back to 'Free delivery' or hide the fee label when data is missing.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' carousel, the third card ('Trattoria Piccol…') and its title are hard-clipped at the right screen edge with no visible peek/padding, making it look broken rather than scrollable.
issues.suggestion: Add consistent horizontal padding and reveal a partial card so the row reads as scrollable; truncate titles with an ellipsis inside the card width.

issues.description: The second 'Popular right now' card (pizza, -20%) is abruptly cut off by the bottom navigation bar with no title/metadata visible, and the content area appears to lack bottom scroll padding.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom padding equal to the nav bar height to the scroll container so the last card can be fully scrolled into view.

issues.description: The favorite (heart) buttons are inconsistent: the first card uses a white circular background with a dark outline heart, while the second uses a dark/translucent circle with a white heart.
issues.suggestion: Standardize the favorite button background, size, and icon color across all restaurant cards.

issues.description: The category chip row is clipped mid-chip at the right edge, showing only a sliver of the next filter with no fade or arrow affordance.
issues.suggestion: Add an edge fade gradient or partial chip visibility with consistent trailing padding to signal horizontal scrolling.

issues.description: The 'See all' links and the promo banner's secondary text ('Use code TALLINN3 …') use light green/low-opacity text that may fall below the 4.5:1 contrast threshold.
issues.suggestion: Darken the green link color and increase opacity of banner subtext to meet WCAG AA contrast.

issues.description: The notification bell with a red dot badge conveys unread state by color/shape only, with no accessible text label or count.
issues.suggestion: Add an accessible label such as 'Notifications, 1 unread' and consider showing a numeric badge.
